verdict.rationale: Logseq's docs confirm notes are stored locally as plain Markdown files and can be exported to Markdown, JSON, EDN, OPML, HTML, etc., giving strong open-format support (logseq-docs-8). However, hands-on community reports say the newer Logseq DB version moves away from plain Markdown storage ('a database format so I can no longer keep all my data as markdown files' — logseq-comm-7), directly undercutting the durability/vendor-independence promise for users on that track, and another user reports generated Markdown isn't cleanly portable to other tools due to extra whitespace (logseq-comm-16). Missing for 10: confirmation that the DB-version's export/interchange formats remain fully open and lossless, and independent verification of markdown interoperability across tools.
